title: Week 1 of MDS
text:
Starting the MDS Chapter (art by @amelicart on ig)


I officially started off my Master of Data Science program this month, and honestly, it feels so nice to be back on the UBC campus! I won’t lie, getting used to the rigorous new schedule and the daily commute has been a bit of an adjustment, but the silver lining is that the drive has given me the perfect excuse to finally get lost in a new sci-fi audiobook. I’ve been listening to Leviathan Wakes by James S. A. Corey (a recommendation from my boyfriend) and I am absolutely loving it so far. It has actually turned into a surprisingly relaxing buffer between home and school.
Beyond the early mornings and the traffic, the start of the semester has been an absolute blast. Orientation week was very fun, and I’ve already met so many amazing new friends in my cohort. Since this program is fast-paced, it has been so wonderful having a solid group of people to study with, hangout with in between lectures, and just navigate this whole graduate school experience together.
Then comes the coursework. With my background in computer science and data science, I was expecting the first week to be a bit of a review, but the assignments and lectures have still been quite enjoyable. All of the professors are incredibly knowledgeable, super nice, and genuinely passionate about their subjects. One professor even gives out sweet treats during lectures! It’s definitely a busy season of transition, but I am so excited for everything this program has in store!

title: About
text:
Background
I grew up in Vancouver, BC my whole life and like to say that I know about good local eats and sweet treats! I recently wrapped up my undergrad at UBC studying Computer Science and Data Science, and I am so excited to be back on campus this fall starting my Master of Data Science! Professionally, I recently worked as a Data Analyst evaluating AI and machine learning systems. I spent a lot of time stress-testing large language models for hallucinations and reasoning faults, which is a pretty fun way to look under the hood of modern AI.


Why Data Science?
If I had to sum it up, Data Science is the perfect sweet spot between logical problem-solving and creative storytelling. During my undergrad, I realized I didn’t just want to write code—I wanted to understand the “why” behind the information we interact with every day. Whether I’m building end-to-end data pipelines, evaluating large language models for reasoning faults, or diving into statistical learning theory, I love the puzzle of turning raw, messy data into something meaningful and actionable. It’s a field that constantly keeps me on my toes, and I am so excited to dive even deeper into the world of machine learning and AI during my Master’s program!


Outside of Data Science
When I’m not writing studying, I’m usually swapping my keyboard for some kind of granny activity. I love making cute amigurumi crochet, making everything from little plushies to full pixel grid panels. I also spend a lot of my downtime in the kitchen baking—my current obsessions are ceremonial matcha checkerboard cookies and a twist on the classic tiramisu with basque cheesecake. If I’m just relaxing, you can probably catch me sitting at my PC curating Spotify playlists for very specific moods, losing my mind playing Riot games, or organizing my entire life into a hyper-detailed Notion dashboard.


About this site
I created this little corner of the internet as both a digital portfolio and a personal sandbox. While a piece of this site actually started out as a class assignment, it has quickly evolved into a space where my technical side and my creative hobbies get to live in the same room!

title: Audrey Tsung
text: Hi, my name is Audrey and I am from Vancouver, BC. I completed a BSc in Computer Science with a minor in Data Science at UBC, where I developed a strong interest in AI/ML systems evaluation and large-scale data workflows. This interest ultimately led me to pursue the Master of Data Science program. This website documents my experiences, learning journey, and personal growth throughout the MDS program.
